stem:
The compound nitrosyl bromide, $\text{NOBr}$, can be formed by the reaction shown.

$$2\text{NO} + \text{Br}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NOBr}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Using oxidation numbers, explain why this reaction is a redox reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Nitrosyl bromide contains a trivalent nitrogen atom.

Draw the 'dot-and-cross' diagram for $\text{NOBr}$. Show outer electrons only.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The rate of the reaction was measured at various concentrations of the two reactants, $\text{NO}$ and $\text{Br}_2$, and the following results were obtained.

| experiment | $[\text{NO}]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{Br}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial rate $/\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 0.03 | 0.02 | $3.4 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| 2 | 0.03 | 0.04 | $6.8 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| 3 | 0.09 | 0.04 | $6.1 \times 10^{-2}$ |
| 4 | 0.12 | 0.06 | to be calculated |

The general form of the rate equation for this reaction is as follows.

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{NO}]^a[\text{Br}_2]^b$$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: What is meant by the term *order of reaction* with respect to a particular reagent?

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use the data in the table to deduce the values of $a$ and $b$ in the rate equation. Show your reasoning.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Use the data in the table to calculate the initial rate for experiment 4.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Use the results of experiment 1 to calculate the rate constant, $k$, for this reaction. Include the units of $k$.

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text: By considering the rate equation, explain why the rate decreases with decreasing temperature.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The reaction between $X$ and $Y$ was studied.

$$2\text{X} + \text{Y} \rightarrow \text{Z}$$

The following sequence of steps is a proposed mechanism for the reaction.

step 1 $2\text{X} \rightarrow \text{V}$
step 2 $\text{V} + \text{Y} \rightarrow \text{Z}$

The general form of the rate equation for this reaction is as follows.

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{X}]^m[\text{Y}]^n$$

Step 1 is the slower step in the mechanism.

Deduce the values of $m$ and $n$ in the rate equation.
